No command-line override is selected.
artifactRequest.question: Explain how grouped cross-validation keeps transformations inside the training folds. Identify the split, fitted preprocessing, estimator, and evaluation flow; inspect implementation before alleging leakage.
artifactRequest.scope: Source-only interpretation of the selected tabular grouped-CV entrypoint; no target import, execution, or legacy static analysis.

reviewEvidence.quote: for fold_train, fold_valid in folds.split(...) ... encoder.fit_transform(inner_train_x, inner_train_y) ... encoder.transform(inner_valid_x)

claims.summary: The outer holdout uses GroupShuffleSplit with group labels and keeps test rows outside fitting.
Five StratifiedGroupKFold splits are generated from the outer-training partition and its groups.
A fresh encoder is instantiated inside each fold and fitted only on inner-training X and y.
Inner-validation features are transformed without validation labels entering the encoder call.
A fresh CatBoost estimator fits the training Pool while the validation Pool controls early stopping.
Fold validation AUC and best iteration are aggregated into mean AUC and median rounds.
A new encoder and booster are refit on all outer-training rows using the CV-derived round count.
The fitted encoder transforms outer-test features, then held-out labels are used for ROC AUC and average precision.
Visible call sites support fold containment, but missing feature and encoder implementations prevent a complete leakage audit.

dataOrigin.answer: CSV loading and partition flow are clear, but feature engineering and split_frame internals are unavailable.

updatedParametersAndFitState.answer: Per-fold encoder and booster fitting, then final refit, are explicit.

losses.answer: This workflow exposes estimator fitting and metrics but no explicit loss computation beyond CatBoost's configured Logloss.
